newsitem.title: UK: London Electric to review investment plans.
newsitem.headline: London Electric to review investment plans.

text.p: British utility London Electricity Plc said on Thursday it would have to re-examine its long-term investment strategy as a result of proposed tax changes announced in the UK budget last month.
The company, posting a decline in first-half profits, said it hoped certain elements of its programmes, such as tunnelling, would be excluded from the proposals.
In November, Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke proposed reducing capital allowances on long-term investments, prompting concern among utilities and other infrastructure-intensive firms.

"A number of significant investment projects are progressing well," London Electricity said, adding that it planned to proceed with its plans to upgrade the electricity network in London's financial district, the City.
The utility's first-half pre-tax profits fell to 69.3 million pounds from 84.5 million in the year-ago period, but came in line with analysts' forecast range of 61.7 to 86.0 million.
The company raised its interim dividend to 14.3 pence per share from 11.5 pence.
